title: Kubernetes doesn't care about Pod names. Here's why
caption: Labels and selectors make Kubernetes tick. How do you organize your labels?

scenes.vo: How does Kubernetes track thousands of Pods without losing its mind? Not by name or IP, but by simple key-value tags.
scenes.heading: LABELS & SELECTORS

scenes.vo: Think of labels like colorful luggage tags stuck on every container. Selectors are the filter that grabs exactly what you need.
scenes.heading: THE ANALOGY

scenes.vo: You slap a label on your Pods, like env equals prod. Then a Service or Deployment uses a selector to find and route traffic to them.
scenes.heading: HOW THEY CONNECT

scenes.vo: Stop searching random names manually. Just filter by label straight from your terminal.
scenes.heading: THE TRICK

scenes.vo: Labels tag objects, selectors group them, and Kubernetes routes effortlessly. Follow for more Kubernetes in plain English.
scenes.heading: LABELS & SELECTORS
